synthesis: HitAlertSettings::kitAlertSettings() (app/Models/Concerns/HitAlertSettings.php:27-44) filters channels with whereJsonLength('settings->notifications->{sms,emails,slack}','>',0). Laravel compiles that to jsonb_array_length(...), which raises 22023 'cannot get array length of a non-array' when a row stores a channel as a JSON OBJECT. A scalar or JSON null raises '...of a scalar' instead; this reconcile confirmed both messages against local Postgres. The query loads every alert_settings row for the kit org's users, so one malformed row aborts subscriber resolution for that hit type across the whole org. cache()->flexible stores nothing when the closure throws, so every hit re-throws. The objects come from app writers that json_encode key-gapped PHP arrays: Collection filter()/unique()->toArray() with no ->values(). The writers are AlertSettingsForm::formatSms/formatEmails/formatSlack (save path) and AlertSetting::removeEmail/removeSms. removeEmail is reached from the EmailController signed unsubscribe routes and the SubscribedAlertsWidget. The DTO and cast pass shapes through unnormalised. The PHP read side (routeNotificationFor*, collect()) handles objects, so only the SQL breaks. Object rows also silently miss the whereJsonContains (@>) unsubscribe-all and widget queries. All four passes agree on a layered fix: (1) a no-throw SQL guard that counts non-empty arrays AND non-empty objects as configured; (2) list normalisation at the AlertSettingSettingsDto chokepoint plus ->values() at each writer; (3) optionally, repair of existing rows. Still open: whether a backfill ships in this ticket, whether the dormant removeSms wrong-source bug is fixed here, the unmeasured prod bad-row inventory (platform.alert_settings is not in the CDC mirror), writers outside this repo, and human sign-off on the customer-facing blast radius.

scope.summary: Stop jsonb_array_length from throwing on non-array channel values so one malformed alert_settings row can no longer suppress an org's hit alerts. Object-shaped rows that have content must keep receiving alerts. Make every writer persist sequential JSON lists by normalising in the DTO and adding ->values() at each writer. A repair of existing rows (dry-run-first artisan command, not a migration) is proposed but awaits a human scope decision. The removeSms wrong-source fix also awaits a scope decision.

proposed_changes.change: In kitAlertSettings(), replace the three whereJsonLength/orWhereJsonLength calls with a raw per-channel 'has content' predicate built by a small private helper looping over sms/emails/slack. Hard requirements (settled): the predicate cannot throw for any JSON type (no bare jsonb_array_length, and no reliance on AND short-circuiting); a non-empty array or non-empty object counts as configured; [], {}, JSON null and a missing key do not. Keep the webhook_url != '' branch, the cache key/TTL and the query shape unchanged. Use literal path segments and no '?' character (PDO placeholder). The exact expression is left to planning. Candidates offered: a CASE on jsonb_typeof (fast); typeof IN ('array','object') AND value NOT IN ('[]','{}') (c2/c3); coalesce(...) NOT IN ('[]','{}','null') (c1).
proposed_changes.reason: The crash site. One bad row currently aborts subscriber resolution for the whole org. Restricting to typeof='array' would silently drop object-shaped subscribers.

proposed_changes.change: Add a private static list normaliser (array -> array_values; null/'' -> []; see notes for the non-empty scalar policy). Apply it to types, clients and notifications.sms/emails/slack in fromArray() AND toJson(), so direct property mutation (removeEmail/removeSms) is covered too. Guard a non-array 'notifications'. Leave webhook_url a string and the constructor unchanged.
proposed_changes.reason: Single chokepoint for the form save (fromArray) and the cast set() (toJson). Legacy rows heal on their next save.

proposed_changes.change: Add ->values() before ->toArray() in removeEmail() and removeSms(). Contingent on Q-removeSms: change removeSms to source routeNotificationForSms() instead of routeNotificationForMail(). Optional hardening from one pass: make routeNotificationFor* null-safe (collect($x ?? [])->values()).
proposed_changes.reason: removeEmail on a non-last address writes {"1":..}; the unsubscribe flow is the likely prod trigger. removeSms (:122-126) currently writes the filtered EMAIL list into the sms slot. It has no callers.

proposed_changes.change: Add ->values() before ->toArray() in formatSms, formatEmails and formatSlack.
proposed_changes.reason: filter() (personal email/phone toggled off, bad slack prefix) and unique() (non-trailing duplicate) preserve keys, so any gap serialises as an object. The existing tests only dedupe a trailing element.

proposed_changes.change: Optional hardening: in get(), pass (json_decode($value ?? '{}', true) ?: []) or an is_array guard to fromArray. Do NOT normalise raw arrays in set(); tests use that path to seed bad shapes.
proposed_changes.reason: A stored jsonb 'null' would TypeError in fromArray(array $data). Verified at AlertSettingsCast.php:15.

questions.q: Is the prod error caused by an object-shaped channel value (vs a scalar/null)?
questions.answer: Yes. jsonb_array_length raises 'non-array' for an object and 'of a scalar' for a string or JSON null. This reconcile confirmed both messages on local Postgres. The ticket shows the object variant, which matches the key-gapped json_encode from filter()/unique()->toArray() (reproduced with php -r).

notes: Guard shape: every candidate expression is equivalent on arrays, objects, [], {}, null and missing. They differ on a non-empty JSON scalar (e.g. "x"): c1's coalesce NOT IN counts it as configured, while fast/c2/c3 exclude it. No writer in the repo produces scalars, and the prod error is the object variant. Planning must pick one policy, keep the DTO list normaliser consistent with it (scalar -> [scalar] vs []), and pin it in a test.

Impact: one bad row blocks L/S (and M) alerts for every subscriber in the org. Nothing is cached on failure, so this is high severity despite only 6 log lines. The Sep 29 onset fits a first bad row created by an unsubscribe or form save around then; that is inference, and activity_log ('Alert Settings Unsubscribe') plus updated_at on the 16 users can confirm it.
The SQL guard, the writer fixes and the repair are complementary. The guard alone leaves bad rows that break @> unsubscribe and types matching; the writer fix alone leaves existing rows throwing.
Object-shaped types would make types @> hit_type silently false (no error, no alerts). Normalise types/clients too, and count them separately in any dry-run.

Test seeding: seed malformed rows with raw JSON via DB::connection('platform')->table('alert_settings') insert/update, because the model/DTO will normalise once fixed. Clear the flexible cache key alert_settings:t:{type}:k:{kit_id} between cases. kitAlertSettings plucks user ids then runs whereIn on platform.alert_settings, which is not a cross-connection join. Extend HitEventListenerTest / HitWebhookFanOutTest harnesses.

Read-only inventory shape for a human (aggregates, then ids/org_id only): SELECT ch, jsonb_typeof(settings->'notifications'->ch), count(*) FROM alert_settings CROSS JOIN (VALUES ('sms'),('emails'),('slack')) v(ch) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL GROUP BY 1,2.

Illustrative ops repair per channel: jsonb_set(settings,'{notifications,<ch>}', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(v) from jsonb_each(settings#>'{notifications,<ch>}') e(k,v)),'[]')) where jsonb_typeof(...)='object'. jsonb_each orders keys by length then bytes; that is harmless for channel lists.

tests.what_it_pins: One org with a valid array row, a raw-inserted object-shaped emails row ({"1":"b@x"}), scalar/JSON-null sms/slack rows, an empty {} row, and a webhook-only row. For L and S (and M), kitAlertSettings/getSubscribers/HitEvent do not throw. The valid row, the object-with-content row and the webhook-only row resolve and are notified (Notification::fake); the empty rows are excluded.
Existing webhook-only coverage still passes after the predicate rewrite.

fromArray/toJson turn gapped or object arrays into lists for types, clients and all three channels. Non-array notifications and scalar/null values follow the chosen policy. The round trip is idempotent and webhook_url is unchanged.
get() on a stored JSON null or non-array does not TypeError. set() with a DTO holding gapped arrays writes JSON arrays.
Unsubscribing the first or middle address of [a,b,c] leaves jsonb_typeof = 'array'. unsubscribeFromAllAlerts works after repeated removals. A legacy object row rewrites as an array.

formatSms/Emails/Slack return array_is_list results when a leading or middle duplicate, an invalid slack URL, or the personal entry (toggle off) is removed. save() persists JSON arrays (assert the raw column).
removeEmail on a non-last element stores an array, and kitAlertSettings then does not throw. If Q-removeSms is approved: removeSms shrinks only sms and leaves emails untouched.
--dry-run writes nothing and reports counts. A real run fixes only non-array rows and leaves healthy rows and updated_at untouched. A second run is a no-op.

data_impact.repair: Only if Q-backfill is approved: rewrite settings JSON for rows whose lists are not arrays. data_impact.cache: No flush is needed. Once a row is repaired, a stale cached subscriber list lasts up to 30 minutes, which is harmless.
